hints: Count the sides and corners after the turn — did either number change?
A shape's sides and corners depend on the shape itself, not which way it is facing.

canonical: Turning the triangle changes which way it points, but not its sides or corners.
It still has 3 sides and 3 corners, so 3 + 3 = 6 altogether.

stem: A triangle has 3 straight sides and 3 corners. It is rotated 1 times, a third of a full turn each time, so its point ends up facing a different way. How many sides and corners does it have now, added together?
